When is Chinese New Year 2027? | Saturday 6 February 2027, the start of the Year of the Goat. Families hold reunion dinners on the evening of Friday 5 February, and shrine events and processions on Samui continue for a few days after.
Where are the lion dances on Koh Samui? | Mainly in Maenam, around the Chinese temple near the pier and the old Chinatown street, which has the most colourful and family-friendly processions. Nathon's Hainanese shrine and the Guan Yu shrine above Hua Thanon also hold lion dances. Times are announced locally in late January.
Is Chinese New Year on Samui suitable for children? | Maenam's lion and dragon dances are the best choice for families. Keep children back from firecrackers and protect their ears. Nathon's traditional rites have included spirit mediums with pierced cheeks, and the large Guan Yu statue can frighten small children.
Are shops and restaurants closed at Chinese New Year on Samui? | Most are open. Chinese New Year is not a national public holiday in Thailand, so banks, ferries, tours and most restaurants run as normal, but some Chinese-owned shops in Nathon and Maenam close for one to three days.
What should I wear to a Chinese shrine on Koh Samui? | Cover your shoulders and knees, as at a Buddhist temple. Red is considered lucky at New Year; plain black and white are associated with mourning. Remove shoes where you see others doing so.
Is February a good time for boat trips from Koh Samui? | Yes, the best of the year. February averages about 64 mm of rain over 4 days, with the calmest sea, so Ang Thong (open from 16 December), Pig Island and Koh Tao trips all run with good visibility.
